response: Yes, serum total bilirubin has been found to be useful in differentiating cardioembolic stroke from other stroke subtypes. Studies have shown that patients with cardioembolic stroke tend to have higher levels of serum total bilirubin compared to those with other stroke subtypes. This is because cardioembolic stroke is often associated with cardiac conditions such as atrial fibrillation, which can lead to increased bilirubin production. Therefore, measuring serum total bilirubin levels may help clinicians differentiate cardioembolic stroke from other types of stroke, such as lacunar or atherosclerotic stroke.
